marks.gloss_en: תניא כוותיה דרב חסדא: כל אלו שאמרו אין מדליקין בהן בשבת מדליקין בהן ביום טוב, חוץ משמן שריפה, לפי שאין שורפין קדשים ביום טוב
the baraita: all those which they said one may not light with on Shabbat, one may light with on a Festival
כתפלה: מה תפלה בהודאה, אף ברכת המזון בהודאה -- as in the prayer, so in Grace after Meals
Hanukkah is mentioned in Grace after Meals (the iba'ya's second horn: because of publicising the miracle)
דאמר רב גידל אמר רב -- as the haftara on Shabbat-Rosh Chodesh omits Rosh Chodesh, so the additional prayer omits Hanukkah
Abaye: this [ruling] of Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda is Rav's
מי דמי? התם נביא בדראש חדש ליכא כלל, הכא איתיה בערבית ושחרית ומנחה -- there a haftara does not exist on Rosh Chodesh at all; here [Hanukkah's mention] is in arvit, shacharit and mincha
אלא להא דמיא -- rather, [Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda's ruling] is comparable to this teaching of Rav: the mincha haftara on a Festival-Shabbat omits the Festival
Rav: when a Festival falls on Shabbat, one who reads the haftara at mincha on Shabbat need not mention the Festival, for were it not Shabbat there would be no haftara at mincha on a Festival
Hanukkah is not mentioned in the additional prayers (the iba'ya's first horn: since it has no additional prayer of its own; the ruling of Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda)
נקוט דרב בידך, דקאי רבי אושעיא כוותיה: days with an additional offering, such as Rosh Chodesh, have mention in Grace after Meals
Rosh Chodesh is mentioned in Grace after Meals
שני וחמישי מאי עבידתייהו? -- Monday and Thursday, what are they doing [in a list of days with their own liturgy]?
אלא שני וחמישי ושני של תעניות ומעמדות -- the Monday-Thursday-Monday of fasts (= p_sheni_shel_taaniyot)
rather: Monday and Thursday and Monday of fasts, and maamadot
